statement: Authenticated PG-wire classifies the exact parameterized service lifecycle SQL family before execution, requires action-specific authorization, defensively carries server-derived identity into SQLQueryEngine dispatch, and returns typed command-owner outcomes without direct catalog or runtime-state ownership.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

The grammar is exactly parameterized INSTALL SERVICE $1, UPGRADE SERVICE $1, REMOVE SERVICE $1, SHOW SERVICE $1, and parameterless SHOW SERVICES, with an optional trailing semicolon. Install and upgrade carry manifest, artifact_source, idempotency_key, and optional config; remove carries service_name and idempotency_key; single-service read carries service_name. Extra tokens, parameters, malformed JSON, unknown fields, and client owner/security fields fail typed.

PG wire classifies lifecycle intent before execution and authorizes distinct service.install, service.upgrade, service.remove, and service.read actions. Unauthenticated, generic-only, and trust-default sessions fail before dispatch. SqlRequest defensively copies and freezes authenticated tenant, principal, and roles and rejects tenant mismatch; direct engine use without canonical context fails before the command owner.

SQL owns grammar and projection only, dispatching normalized commands to the composed service lifecycle command owner. SQL issues no direct service catalog mutations, infers no runtime success, reports recorded_not_running truthfully, and rejects lifecycle mutation inside SQL transactions or when command composition is unavailable.

Password-mode PG-wire production policy includes the four lifecycle actions, trust mode retains only generic query authorization, and shared bootstrap's live SQLQueryEngine setter is the production composition seam. No feature flag, WebSocket fallback, direct-table fallback, or CLI behavior is added.

The scenario proves unauthenticated and generic-only rejection, trust-default rejection, malformed grammar/payload and spoof rejection, missing owner/context rejection, transactional mutation rejection, unresolved artifacts without writes, idempotency replay/collision, tenant isolation, and truthful install, upgrade, remove, and SHOW projections through the real command and catalog owners.

Production changes are limited to src/query and src/runtime; tests, one scenario runner, and architecture/service-control-transport.md plus architecture/lagrange-service-registry.md may cover and document the boundary. Command/catalog owner implementation, reconciliation, runtime activation, CLI behavior, provider credentials, and actual-state owners are excluded.

Independent verification must approve the exact source patch and aggregate fingerprint and show the scenario turns red when lifecycle authorization is downgraded to generic query, when authenticated context propagation is removed, or when SQL bypasses the catalog command owner.
